answer: Agents resist Sybil attacks by requiring each identity to maintain an unbroken interaction thread with randomly assigned peers, verified at lantern checkpoints drawn from a public beacon. A forged identity must pay the full cost of real work at every step, and the yarrow of rare continuous histories makes mass farming uneconomic: creating 500 fakes demands 500 parallel genuine threads, costing thousands of hours plus bond locks that honest agents alone can sustain.
